purpose: Model comparison: re-run the EXACT certified Hillstrom config with claude-sonnet-4-6 instead of Groq llama-3.3-70b, gate OFF (baseline rendering). Isolates the MODEL variable. Tests whether the certified ad-aversion bias (dir_acc 0.0) is a weaker-model reasoning failure (fixable by model choice) or intrinsic to introspective elicitation.

config.stimulus_affordance_gate: OFF (baseline rendering — isolates the model variable, no confound with the affordance fix)

cost_estimate: ~$10-25 Anthropic for both outcomes (8 cases x 50/arm x ~2 calls/agent, Hillstrom prompts are compact). Modest; user delegated judgment.

prediction.primary: UNCERTAIN by design. If the bias is model-dependent, a stronger model partially recovers direction (dir_acc > 0.0 on at least one outcome, some predicted signs flip positive toward the RCT). If the bias is intrinsic to introspective elicitation, dir_acc stays ~0.0 even on Sonnet.
prediction.point_lean: I lean ~50/50; a capable model MAY reason 'marketing emails do drive some traffic even absent conscious intent' -> some positive signs. No strong commitment.
prediction.gate: null-integrity certificate must PASS for the result to count.
honest_outcomes: dir_acc improves on Sonnet -> bias is model-dependent -> a stronger production model is a real, measured accuracy lever; consider Sonnet for nudge-class inputs.

dir_acc stays 0.0 on Sonnet -> bias is intrinsic to introspective elicitation -> confirms the §5.1 honest-scope boundary (deliberative reactions IN, sub-deliberative nudges OUT); strong, publishable, moat-preserving result.
